title: 1953 Kingman crash and Upshot-Knothole

tellings.quote: You have uh testimonies like the 1953 Kingman Arizona crash where possibly nuclear testing from operation upshot not hole mess with craft.
I just want to say that that there's no question in my mind that Kingman was the real thing.
tellings.difference: Dolan just says Kingman was real, crediting Raymond Fowler, and says nothing about Upshot-Knothole testing bringing the craft down.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the 1953 Kingman, Arizona crash as a real crash retrieval; the story's telling adds only a possible nuclear-test cause.

plain: A craft of unknown origin is said to have crashed near Kingman, Arizona, in 1953, and one teller suggests that US nuclear tests that year, a series called Operation Upshot-Knothole, may have interfered with it. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb lists it among the "testimonies" of crashes and says the testing "possibly" messed with the craft, without naming a source. Richard Dolan, a historian of UFO cases, tells Michels "there's no question in my mind that Kingman was the real thing," crediting the UFO researcher Raymond Fowler, but he says nothing about the nuclear tests. If true, it would mean the government recovered a crashed craft decades ago.
